A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, retaining its alignment framework and original experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original measurements of CNN alignment across layers, training, random rotations and distribution shifts, including Table 1, Figures 1–6 and appendix Figure A1.

after.justification: V2 retains original CNN results and adds original alignment analyses of self-supervised networks, brain responses, vision transformers and language-model checkpoints in Appendices A4–A8.

M1.justification: The permutation/soft-matching, Procrustes and linear alignment objectives remain unchanged, as does CNN center-pixel extraction. The additional studies apply this framework to other systems; their representation selection and normalization introduce evaluation settings rather than a new alignment algorithm.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained CIFAR100, ImageNet and 17 OOD datasets, v2 adds inter-subject fMRI alignment using the Natural Scenes Dataset and language-representation analysis using Pile-trained Pythia models on STSB sentences. It also adds self-supervised contrastive training on ImageNet. ViTs extend model coverage on the existing visual datasets.

E2.justification: The evaluated alignment-method set remains linear regression, Procrustes and permutation/soft matching. MoCo, ViT and Pythia are additional systems being analyzed. Newly discussed approaches such as model stitching are not added as evaluated alignment baselines.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce checkpoint-to-fully-trained-reference comparisons, 50-epoch MoCo training, 25-epoch ViT training with batch size 32 and CLS-token representations, noise-ceiling-normalized fMRI analysis of four subjects and 1,000 shared images, and analysis of 154 Pythia checkpoints. The original CNN training budgets and five-fold cross-validation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A4 adds a fully trained reference control to examine whether early agreement merely reflects networks following similar developmental trajectories. A5 tests robustness to self-supervised training, including OOD and rotation analyses. A7 extends the rotation control to ViTs and finds that CNN axis preservation does not generalize.

E5.justification: A6 adds noise-ceiling estimation from three repeated stimulus measurements and standard deviations across six participant pairs. Conversely, v2 removes Figure 6's explanation that its error bars represent variability in leave-one-dataset-out correlations, although the plotted bars remain. The original CNN seed-pair setup and five-fold reporting practice are retained.

E6.justification: New findings include MoCo's 14.87% mean rotation penalty, a larger linear–Procrustes gap in brain data, absent rotation penalties in ViTs, and language alignment without the CNN-like depth decline (Figures A3–A6). Figure 4 adds four within-architecture training series. Figure A2 adds fixed-reference trajectories, some continuing to rise beyond epoch one. Table 1 and most original figure results are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical alignment definitions, mapping constraints and complexity discussion are retained. New discussion of silent alignment, deep linear networks and neural tangent kernels supplies context and future directions, without adding formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, key contributions and Discussion retain the central claims about alignment under increasingly flexible transformations, very early convergence and contrasting early/deep-layer behavior under distribution shift. The large-scale-audit framing and additional appendix evidence do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive qualifications involving ViT axis variability and initialization artifacts, language models' different depth profile, and anatomical or ROI-related explanations for the brain data's greater need for flexible transformations. The Discussion removes the unequal-learning-speed caveat and adds the absence of a theoretical account, with NTK-based analysis proposed as future work.

D1.justification: The new appendices disclose selected technical details, including ViT patch and batch sizes, CLS extraction, MoCo training duration, NSD subject IDs and ROI definitions, and Pythia model sizes and checkpoint selection. The original Xavier initialization and CNN training schedule are relocated to A1 unchanged; no new code-access or hardware information is supplied.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands the research context with silent alignment, lazy/rich learning dynamics, NTKs, model stitching and relative representations. It also introduces sources for NSD, MoCo, ViTs, Pythia, the Pile and STSB, situating the expanded analyses beyond the original CNN-focused literature.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, and the introduction, evaluation description, results discussion and limitations receive substantial editing. Sections become numbered, evaluation is organized into four regimes, network-training details move to Appendix A1, and references move after the expanded appendices.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout and adds Figures A2–A6. The training figure is redrawn with ten model-pair series instead of six, existing figures are repositioned and renumbered, and Figure A1's panels are rearranged. Table 1 is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence about which convergence patterns generalize: A5–A8 test additional learning regimes, architectures and biological data while exposing exceptions to the CNN findings. A4 also directly examines alignment with mature representations. These gains improve the study's empirical grounding, although some fixed-reference trajectories do not support its strongest first-epoch wording, and Figure 6 loses its uncertainty explanation.
